response:
Diagnosis. Generation 6 produced a decisive result: replacing EBITDA with R&D-added-back EBITDA in the profitability leg lifted every statistic simultaneously (Innovation Adjusted Profit Less Rollover: fmb 4.76, alpha 4.5%, t 4.01, Sharpe 0.28, coverage 0.124 — the archive's best on all four). The second-best result was the three-leg construct with the idiosyncratic (industry-adjusted) decay penalty (alpha 4.2%, t 3.90). So the two most productive axes are now (i) *measurement of the profitability leg* — expensed investment is being mistakenly netted out of operating strength — and (ii) *decay decomposed into firm-specific versus cyclical*. Conversely, the supplier-days leg destroyed alpha (0.9%), and the accrual conditioner and hard solvency gate both produced zero or negative alpha, so those channels are closed. With two generations left, this batch consolidates on the winning profit-leg measurement (union with the decay leg, a further step up the income statement, a cash-flow version, and a multi-year version) while spending one slot on a genuinely new interaction — the risk that refinancing pressure forces an R&D-dependent firm to cut its innovation — and one slot on the decomposition diagnostic that determines whether the R&D gain is a measurement correction or simply an added intangible-intensity factor.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Innovation Profit Less Rollover Less Idiosyncratic Decay
EXPRESSION: SUB(SUB(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(oibdp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(dlc, act), 1))), ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(IND_ADJ(DELTA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1))), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Durable operating strength is high investment-adjusted profitability relative to industry peers, unthreatened by near-term refinancing needs and not eroding faster than the industry cycle explains; the three conditions are economically distinct and should compound.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This unites the two best gen-6 findings, which improved along independent axes — the profit-leg measurement correction (fmb 4.76, alpha 4.5%) and the cyclically-purged decay penalty (alpha 4.2%, t 3.90) — so it is the single highest-value untested point for joint strength rather than a parameter variant. All legs are winsorized and unit-standardized, and the decay leg is a symmetric first difference rather than the zero-inflated drawdown product, so the composite should retain a strong cross-sectional slope.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Profit Plus Research Intensity Less Rollover
EXPRESSION: SUB(ADD(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 1))), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(dlc, act), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: If adding research spending back to operating profit works because expensing understates durable earning power, then unbundling the two — margin and research intensity as separate standardized channels — should be at least as informative and reveals whether the gain is a measurement correction or an independent intangible-intensity premium.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The gen-6 jump from adding xrd into the numerator was large enough that its interpretation determines how the final signal should be built, and the constrained one-for-one add-back is only optimal if the two components deserve identical weights. Unbundling also lets research intensity contribute where margins are noisy, and comparing this against Signal 1 and the gen-6 leader identifies whether R&D belongs inside the profitability measure or beside it.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Gross Investment Profit Less Rollover
EXPRESSION: SUB(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(SUB(revt, cogs), COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(dlc, act), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Moving further up the income statement — gross profit plus research spending, before all discretionary overhead — measures the productive capability of the asset base with the least managerial-discretion contamination, and that capability is what must be judged against refinancing pressure.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The R&D add-back result implies that items which are investments in disguise should not be netted out of operating strength; selling and administrative expense contains brand-building and distribution investment for the same reason, so this tests the logical endpoint of that argument on the winning two-leg architecture. If it beats the gen-6 leader, the final consolidation should use gross-plus-research profitability; if it does not, the discretionary-overhead line genuinely carries information about durable efficiency.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Profit Less Innovation Funding Risk
EXPRESSION: SUB(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(oibdp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(MUL(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), RATIO(dlc, act)), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: A research-intensive firm facing near-term debt maturities out of thin liquid assets will cut the very spending that sustains its franchise, so refinancing pressure is far more damaging to durable profitability when the firm's earning power depends on a discretionary innovation program than when it does not.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This is a new interaction rather than a new leg: the fragility term is zero for non-innovators and grows only where funding pressure and research dependence co-occur, capturing an adjustment-cost channel (forced abandonment of intangible investment) that no balance-sheet or margin-decay measure represents. It also complements Signal 1 by asking whether R&D belongs in the *penalty* as a source of vulnerability as well as in the profit measure as understated strength.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Cash Plus Research Profit Less Rollover
EXPRESSION: SUB(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(oancf, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(dlc, act), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: The cleanest measure of durable operating strength is the cash the business generates before discretionary innovation spending, since cash — not accrual profit — is what services maturing claims and funds the research program that sustains the franchise.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Profit-leg measurement is now the archive's most productive axis, and the one cash-based construct tested delivered the best Sharpe on record (0.44) before coverage limitations obscured it; pairing operating cash flow with the R&D add-back tests whether the accrual/cash distinction adds to the investment-measurement correction. Coverage will be lower because oancf begins later in the sample, so its statistics must be read alongside Signal 1 rather than on their own.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Industry Cumulative Earning Power Less Rollover
EXPRESSION: SUB(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(TS_SUM(ADD(oibdp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), 5), lt), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(dlc, act), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Persistent earning power is best measured as five years of accumulated investment-adjusted operating profit relative to the current stock of creditor claims, judged against industry peers whose capital intensity and normal payback horizons differ.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The gen-6 cumulative-flow version had the second-best FMB slope in the archive (3.84) despite lacking both the industry adjustment and the R&D correction that have since proven decisive, so applying both to it is the natural consolidation of the persistence channel. Comparing it with Signal 1 separates whether the payoff comes from a durable multi-year record of profit relative to obligations or from the current year's margin advantage.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---CRITIQUE Innovation Profit Less Rollover Less Idiosyncratic Decay---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Internally consistent (the NEG(IND_ADJ(DELTA)) leg correctly penalizes idiosyncratic margin decline) and the sign logic holds, but it is a mechanical union of two already-tested archive signals rather than a new economic idea, so its informational value is limited to confirming whether the two adjustments are additive.

---CRITIQUE Profit Plus Research Intensity Less Rollover---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The unbundling diagnostic is legitimate and answers a real question about the gen-6 jump, but the freed R&D/assets leg is close to the published R&D-intensity premium, and COALESCE(xrd,0) conflates non-reporters with zero-R&D firms, so a positive result will be hard to attribute to the intended mechanism.

---CRITIQUE Gross Investment Profit Less Rollover---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: Construction is internally inconsistent — R&D sits below the gross-profit line (typically inside xsga), so revt−cogs never deducted it and adding xrd back double-credits research spending, on top of the profit leg being essentially the published gross-profitability anomaly.

---CRITIQUE Profit Less Innovation Funding Risk---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 4
RATIONALE: A genuinely new and economically coherent interaction (forced abandonment of intangible investment under refinancing pressure) with the penalty correctly zero for non-innovators, though replacing rather than supplementing the standalone rollover leg risks discarding the archive's most reliable penalty for the ~half of firms with no R&D.

---CRITIQUE Cash Plus Research Profit Less Rollover---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 4
RATIONALE: Consistent construction (oancf does expense R&D, so the add-back is not double-counting) and a substantive test of whether the cash/accrual distinction is separate from the investment-measurement correction, with the acknowledged caveat that it partly overlaps the published cash-based operating profitability factor and will face reduced coverage.

---CRITIQUE Industry Cumulative Earning Power Less Rollover---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Economically coherent and the liabilities denominator makes it more than a cosmetic tweak, but it is largely an archived signal (Cumulative Earning Power Versus Claims) with two already-proven adjustments bolted on, so the expected marginal learning is modest and any gain may reflect the leverage-scaled denominator rather than the persistence channel.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Intangible Capital Adjusted Profit Less Rollover
EXPRESSION: SUB(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(oibdp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), ADD(at, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5))), 1)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(dlc, act), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: If research spending is an investment rather than an expense, then consistency requires treating it as investment on both sides of the profitability ratio: adding it back to operating profit *and* capitalizing the accumulated research stock into the capital base, so that innovators are neither penalized in the numerator nor flattered by an understated denominator.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio
REASONING: This removes the double-crediting error — R&D is added back only once, to a profit measure (oibdp) from which it genuinely was deducted — and replaces the published gross-profitability leg with an economically coherent return-on-invested-capital measure whose denominator includes five years of capitalized research. It is the natural completion of the gen-6 finding that drove the archive's best result (fmb 4.76, alpha 4.5%): if the correction belongs on both sides of the ratio, this should dominate the numerator-only version, and if it does not, the earlier gain was an intangible-intensity tilt rather than a measurement fix.
